features.label: Runs more than one kind of agent
features.description: Can drive more than one coding agent (Claude Code, Codex and so on) side by side.

features.label: Coding agents supported
features.description: How many different coding agents it can run, per its own docs.

features.label: Alerts when you're needed
features.description: How it tells you an agent is waiting on you.

features.label: Answer "Allow?" prompts from the manager
features.description: When an agent stops to ask permission (run this command? edit this file?), you can allow or deny it from the manager or your phone instead of opening that agent's own window.

features.label: Hand-offs between agents in one view
features.description: Work passed from one agent to another shows up in the same place.

features.label: Always-on assistant
features.description: A standing assistant session you can reach any time.

features.label: Chat view of a session
features.description: Read a session as a conversation instead of raw terminal text.

features.label: Open the real terminal
features.description: Drop into the session's actual terminal.

features.label: How sessions are organized
features.description: List, worktrees, kanban or nested groups.

features.label: Prompt drafts
features.description: Draft prompts and insert them without sending.

features.label: Saved prompts
features.description: Reusable prompts you can fire with context attached.

features.label: Built-in editor / browser
features.description: Ships its own editor or browser.

features.label: Look and font control
features.description: How far you can change its look, including your terminal's font.

features.label: Shows your usage limits
features.description: Your subscription usage and resets, read from local logs.

features.label: Predicts when you'll hit a limit
features.description: Burn rate and time to the limit, not just current usage.

features.label: Pause and resume at usage limits
features.description: Pauses work near a limit and picks it back up after the reset.

features.label: Switch accounts without logging in again
features.description: Move between provider accounts without re-login.

features.label: Tasks from your notes vault
features.description: Reads your own notes vault (such as Obsidian) as the task list.

features.label: Turns GitHub or Jira issues into pull requests
features.description: Picks up an issue from GitHub, GitLab, Linear or Jira, hands it to an agent, and carries the resulting pull request through review.

features.label: Manages git worktrees
features.description: Gives each agent or task its own git worktree.

features.label: Planner that splits the work
features.description: Breaks a goal into parts and runs them.

features.label: Agents message each other
features.description: One session can message or query another.

features.label: Knowledge base for agents
features.description: A notes store agents can look things up in.

features.label: Phone app
features.description: A dedicated iOS or Android app.

features.label: Phone access with no new app
features.description: Reach it from your phone with tools you already have.

features.label: Remote machines over SSH
features.description: Run or edit sessions on another machine.

features.label: Voice input
features.description: Dictate to it.

features.label: Operating systems
features.description: Which systems it runs on, plus phone or browser access, per its own release files or docs.

features.label: App shell
features.description: What the app is built on: Electron, Tauri, a terminal UI, or a hosted service.

features.label: Main languages
features.description: Top languages in its repo, from GitHub's breakdown.

features.label: Background process
features.description: Whether it runs a separate server or daemon next to the app.

features.label: Download size
features.description: Installer size from its latest release. Not memory use.

features.description: Size as a share of Claude Desktop, which measured about 7.5 GB on one Windows PC on 2026-09-28 (about 3.7 GB for the app across 24 processes, plus about 4 GB for the virtual machine it starts for Cowork). The coding agents themselves cost the same under every tool.

features.label: Runs in your own terminal
features.description: Lives inside the terminal you already use.

features.label: License / cost
features.description: Open-source license or pricing.

features.label: Plugins / SDK
features.description: Outside developers can extend it.

features.label: Teams
features.description: Built for more than one person.

features.label: Maturity

tools.name: vibe-kanban
tools.where_agents_run: your machine (desktop app or a local web server opened in your browser); a self-hosted server you reach through a tunnel; phone or another computer through the browser after pairing
tools.source_note: Checked against its README, docs/ folder, source code, releases (last stable v0.1.44, 2026-04-24; npx-only v0.1.45 prerelease, 2026-09-19) and the shutdown announcement at vibekanban.com/blog/shutdown. The company announced a sunset on 2026-04-10; the kanban board and hosted issues were retired in v0.1.44 and the project is now community maintained. Not installed or run here.

multi_provider_supervision.value: Pick a different coding agent per workspace or session and run them side by side; the app reads each agent's output into its own chat view (README and docs, 2026-09-29)

harness_count.value: 10 per its docs: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Amp, Cursor Agent, OpenCode, Droid, Claude Code Router, Qwen Code (docs/supported-coding-agents.mdx, 2026-09-29)

needs_you_signal.value: Sound effects and system notifications when a task finishes, needs attention or errors; approval cards in the chat (docs/settings/general.mdx and source, 2026-09-29)

approve_deny_prompt.value: Tool-permission and plan approvals from the agent appear as cards in the app's chat to approve or deny; wired for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot and the agents it drives through the Agent Client Protocol, such as Gemini and Qwen; unanswered requests time out (docs/workspaces/chat-interface.mdx and crates/executors source, 2026-09-29)

cross_provider_delegation.value: Has sessions with different agents inside one workspace, sharing its files, and an MCP server an agent can use to start another agent's workspace; lacks a view that tracks a hand-off from one agent to another, and sessions do not share conversation context (docs/workspaces/sessions.mdx and docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx, 2026-09-29)

conversation_gui_view.value: Each session is a chat: agent replies rendered as formatted text, tool calls and system messages styled separately, edit and resend, a queue for follow-ups (docs/workspaces/chat-interface.mdx, 2026-09-29)

real_terminal.value: Has an xterm.js terminal in each workspace's sidebar for your own commands; lacks the agent's own terminal, since agents run in the background and are shown only as chat and logs (docs/workspaces/interface.mdx and crates/executors source, 2026-09-29)

session_organization.value: Workspaces (one git worktree and branch each, pinned or archived) holding one or more chat sessions; the kanban board that grouped them was retired in v0.1.44 and now shows only a data-export page (docs and pull request 3387, 2026-09-29)

prompt_scratchpad.value: Has an unsent follow-up message saved as a draft per session, plus a queue that holds a message until the agent finishes; lacks a separate place to keep several prompt drafts (source useSessionMessageEditor.ts and docs/workspaces/chat-interface.mdx, 2026-09-29)

saved_prompt_library.value: Has task tags: reusable text snippets inserted with @ into a task description; lacks context attached to a saved prompt (docs/configuration-customisation/creating-task-tags.mdx, 2026-09-29)

builtin_editors_browser.value: Built-in browser preview of your app with devtools, inspect mode and device emulation, plus a diff viewer with inline comments; files open in your own editor (README and docs, 2026-09-29)

appearance_control.value: Has light and dark themes and an interface language setting; lacks font or terminal font settings in its docs (docs/settings/general.mdx, 2026-09-29)

usage_hud.value: Has a context gauge per session (tokens used of the model's window) and, in Codex sessions, a status command that reads the account's rate limits; lacks Claude plan limits and a running usage display (docs/workspaces/chat-interface.mdx and codex slash_commands.rs, 2026-09-29)

burn_rate_forecast.value: No burn rate or time-to-limit; source search for rate-limit handling finds only the Codex status command and a Claude event it ignores (source, 2026-09-29)

vault_task_source.value: Tasks came from its own kanban issues (now retired); a source search finds no notes-vault or Obsidian reader (source, 2026-09-29)

issue_tracker_pipeline.value: Has pull request creation with generated descriptions and merge through the GitHub command-line tool, and Azure Repos support; lacks a connection that pulls issues from GitHub, Linear or Jira, and its own issue board was retired in v0.1.44 (docs/integrations and pull request 3387, 2026-09-29)

worktree_management.value: Every workspace gets its own git worktree and branch, with rebase, conflict help, merge and cleanup of old worktrees (docs/workspaces and README, 2026-09-29)

planner_orchestrator.value: Has an MCP server an outside agent can use to split a plan into issues and start a workspace per issue; lacks a built-in planner, and the issue tools depended on the retired hosted projects (docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx and shutdown notice, 2026-09-29)

agent_to_agent_messaging.value: Its MCP server lets an agent start workspaces, create sessions, send a prompt into another session and read its final message (docs/integrations/vibe-kanban-mcp-server.mdx, 2026-09-29)

knowledge_base.value: Not in its docs (checked 2026-09-29); per-workspace notes exist for you, and the docs don't say agents can read them

native_mobile_app.value: No iOS or Android app in the repo; phone access is through the browser (repo search for mobile app frameworks, 2026-09-29)

phone_no_new_app.value: Docs describe pairing a phone browser to your computer through cloud.vibekanban.com; the shutdown notice ended hosted services 30 days after 2026-04-10, the site still loads, and whether pairing still works was not tested (docs/remote-access.mdx and shutdown notice, 2026-09-29)

remote_ssh.value: Has running it on a remote server reached through a tunnel, with "Open in VS Code" links that connect over SSH; lacks running agents on another machine from your local app (README and docs/settings/general.mdx, 2026-09-29)

voice_input.value: No dictation: a source search for speech or voice input in the web app finds nothing (source, 2026-09-29)

os.value: Windows, macOS, Linux (x64 and ARM64 installers each); any of them through npx with Node 20.19 or later; other devices through a browser (v0.1.44 release files and npx-cli/package.json, 2026-09-29)

app_shell.value: Tauri 2.10.3 desktop app, or a local web server opened in your browser through npx; React 18 interface (Cargo.lock and package.json, 2026-09-29)

tools.name: T3 Code
tools.where_agents_run: your machine + another machine you pair or reach over SSH (Linux or Apple Silicon Mac); phone, browser or another desktop app control it through T3 Connect, Tailscale or a local network
tools.source_note: Checked against its README, docs/ folder, source code at commit 4222485, latest stable release (v0.0.43) and t3.codes. Not installed or run here.

multi_provider_supervision.value: Runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode and Google Antigravity threads side by side in one sidebar, using your own logins (README, 2026-09-29)

harness_count.value: 6: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity (README, 2026-09-29)

needs_you_signal.value: Sidebar status per thread (amber for approval, indigo for a question, sky blue while working), desktop notifications with optional sound and an unread badge; phone push when an agent finishes, fails, needs approval or asks something, which needs T3 Connect (source and docs/user/mobile-notifications.md, 2026-09-29)

approve_deny_prompt.value: Approve or reject requests in the conversation on desktop, web or the phone app; the default mode for new threads is Full access, so prompts appear only in Supervised, Auto-accept edits or Auto mode (docs/user/permission-modes.md and mobile source, 2026-09-29)

cross_provider_delegation.value: Has threads from every provider in one sidebar and can send one prompt to several models at once, each in its own thread and worktree; lacks a documented hand-off of work from one agent to another (docs/user/thread-sidebar.md, 2026-09-29)

conversation_gui_view.value: Threads read as a chat with tool calls you can expand to see the full command and output (docs/user/thread-sidebar.md, 2026-09-29)

real_terminal.value: Has a terminal drawer per thread that opens a shell on the environment's machine, 5,000 lines of scrollback; lacks the agent's own terminal screen, because agents are driven through their programming interfaces (Claude Agent SDK, Codex app server, ACP) rather than a terminal (docs/user/terminal.md and package files, 2026-09-29)

session_organization.value: Projects, then threads in pinned, active, snoozed and settled sections, with an optional git worktree per thread and drag-to-reorder; projects can be grouped across machines (docs/user/thread-sidebar.md, 2026-09-29)

prompt_scratchpad.value: Prompt stash: Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) saves the current prompt and its attachments for later without sending (docs/user/composer.md, 2026-09-29)

saved_prompt_library.value: Has the prompt stash, which keeps prompts with their attached context, plus the agents' own skills through a $ menu; lacks a named, lasting library, and uploaded files in a stash expire after 24 hours (docs/user/composer.md, 2026-09-29)

builtin_editors_browser.value: File browser with an editor that saves files, a diff viewer, a preview browser that agents can also drive, and an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator panel (docs/user/devices.md and source, 2026-09-29)

appearance_control.value: Built-in and custom themes (VS Code themes import), light and dark modes, and font family and size for interface, code and terminal (docs/user/appearance.md and apps/web/src/appearanceFonts.ts, 2026-09-29)

usage_hud.value: Usage page with tokens and estimated cost per provider from local history, plus subscription limits with reset times for Codex, Claude and others, pooled across accounts and machines (docs/user/usage.md, 2026-09-29)

burn_rate_forecast.value: Has a pace mark per limit window (ahead of pace, on pace, under pace); lacks a predicted time when you will hit the limit (packages/shared/src/usageLimits.ts, 2026-09-29)

account_hotswap.value: Several Codex or Claude accounts added as separate provider instances and picked from the thread's model picker; switching inside an existing thread only works between accounts that share a config folder (docs/user/providers-codex.md and providers-claude.md, 2026-09-29)

vault_task_source.value: Tasks come from prompts you type; a source and docs search found no notes-vault or Obsidian reading (source search, 2026-09-29)

issue_tracker_pipeline.value: Has pull request creation, review, stacking and merging for GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Gitea, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, and auto-settles a thread when its pull request merges; lacks picking up issues from a tracker, with no issue or Jira/Linear code found in the source (docs/user/source-control.md and source search, 2026-09-29)

worktree_management.value: New worktree per thread from the composer, one per model when sending to several; revert can restore files in a worktree (docs/user/thread-sidebar.md and composer.md, 2026-09-29)

planner_orchestrator.value: Has a Plan mode that shows the agent's proposed plan as a card you can copy or download, and an Agents view for an agent's own subagents; lacks splitting one goal across several agents (docs/user/composer.md, thread-sidebar.md and source, 2026-09-29)

agent_to_agent_messaging.value: The tools it gives agents cover the preview browser, devices and linking pull requests only; nothing lets one thread message another (apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits, 2026-09-29)

native_mobile_app.value: iOS app in the App Store and Android app in Google Play, with home-screen usage widgets and live activity cards (README and docs/user/usage.md, 2026-09-29)

phone_no_new_app.value: Hosted web app at app.t3.codes or a direct pairing link in the phone's browser; needs the server reachable over HTTPS, for example through Tailscale HTTPS or T3 Connect (docs/user/remote-access.md, 2026-09-29)

remote_ssh.value: Desktop-managed SSH: enter a host and it installs or reuses its server there and forwards the port; projects and logins stay on the remote machine (Linux or Apple Silicon Mac) (docs/user/remote-access.md, 2026-09-29)

voice_input.value: Has on-device dictation in the iPhone app (iOS 26 or later); lacks it on desktop, web and Android (docs/user/composer.md and docs/internals/voice-input.md, 2026-09-29)

os.value: Windows, macOS, Linux (x64 and ARM64 each); iOS and Android apps; web app in any browser (release files and README, 2026-09-29)

app_shell.value: Electron 44.4.2 with a React 19.2.6 interface; the same interface also runs as a web app served by its command-line server (apps/desktop/package.json and apps/web/package.json, 2026-09-29)

background_process.value: Yes: the desktop app bundles and starts its own server, which owns agents, terminals and git; the command-line version can install that server as a user service on Linux and macOS (docs/internals/overview.md and docs/user/background-service.md, 2026-09-29)

download_size.value: v0.0.43: 209 MB Windows x64 installer, 143-150 MB mac dmg, 125 MB Linux .deb / 158 MB AppImage; command-line server alone 61-73 MB (GitHub release, 2026-09-29)

ram_vs_claude_desktop.value: Medium (estimate: Electron app plus a bundled Node server process)

runs_in_terminal.value: Own desktop, web and phone apps; the t3 command starts a server and opens the web app rather than showing an interface in the terminal (README, 2026-09-29)

license_cost.value: MIT, free, no paid plan listed; uses your own agent subscriptions (LICENSE and t3.codes, 2026-09-29)

extensibility.value: No plugin system or SDK in its docs or source; outside additions are limited to custom theme files (docs/user/appearance.md and source search, 2026-09-29)

teams_multiuser.value: Not in its docs (checked 2026-09-29); pairing links authorize more devices, not more people

burn_rate_forecast.value: No coding-agent usage tracking in its source, so no forecast (source search, 2026-09-29)

limit_governor.value: No coding-agent limit handling in its source; its limit code covers only its own Wave AI panel (source search, 2026-09-29)

worktree_management.value: The word worktree appears nowhere in its source or docs (source search, 2026-09-29)

planner_orchestrator.value: Not in its docs (checked 2026-09-29); its roadmap lists letting its AI open new blocks as planned

knowledge_base.value: Not in its docs (checked 2026-09-29); its roadmap plans markdown context files for its own Wave AI panel only
